```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 6.5,
  fig.height = 4
)
```

`scale_space_energy()` tests a planned statistic map across a prespecified
resolution continuum. The low-level API deliberately follows the rest of
`neurothresh`: the inferential engine consumes an observed statistic map plus a
calibrated null generator.

There are two related but distinct questions:

* **Localization:** at what resolution can an effect be detected?
* **Frequency readout:** at what spatial band is the effect strongest?

`local_energy()` answers the first question. For the second, use
`global_lowpass_energy()` or `global_band_energy()`.

```{r simulate-subject-images}
library(neurothresh)

set.seed(1)
dims <- c(12, 12, 12)
signal_mask <- array(FALSE, dims)
signal_mask[4:9, 4:9, 4:9] <- TRUE
subject_images <- replicate(
  8,
  {
    img <- array(rnorm(prod(dims), sd = 0.5), dim = dims)
    img[signal_mask] <- img[signal_mask] + 3
    img
  },
  simplify = FALSE
)
```

For a one-sample planned contrast, the raw-image wrapper builds the group map
and deterministic subject-level sign-flip null maps, then calls the same
low-level scanner. The `n_perm` values used below are kept tiny so the
vignette builds quickly: with `B = 19` permutations the smallest possible
corrected p-value is `1/(B + 1) = 0.05`, which is far too coarse for real
analyses. Production runs should use at least `n_perm = 1000`, and 5,000 to
10,000 if power is a concern.

```{r fit-one-sample-scale-space}
fit <- scale_space_onesample(
  subject_images,
  scales = scale_space(
    fwhm_mm = c(4, 8, 12),
    include_global = TRUE,
    include_identity = TRUE
  ),
  statistics = list(
    global_lowpass_energy(),
    global_band_energy(),
    local_energy(),
    signed_coherence(tail = "two")
  ),
  n_perm = 19,
  seed = 1,
  alpha = 0.1
)

fit
head(summary(fit))
```

```{r one-sample-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(fit, "scale_space_energy_result"))
stopifnot(is.data.frame(summary(fit)))
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$selected$best$p_fwer[1]))
stopifnot(fit$selected$best$p_fwer[1] >= 0, fit$selected$best$p_fwer[1] <= 1)
```

The result controls familywise error over spatial scale, location, and requested
statistic channels. The global endpoint is a distributed energy test. The
identity endpoint is the voxelwise limit. Intermediate FWHM values ask whether
the effect is detectable at that localization scale.

```{r resolution-summary}
resolution <- plot_resolution_curve(fit)
resolution[, c("scale_label", "channel", "min_p", "any_supported", "curve_use")]
```

`scale_space_diagnostics()` labels each curve by its intended interpretation.
This is useful because a local-energy curve should not be read as a pure
spatial-frequency spectrum.

```{r scale-space-diagnostics}
scale_space_diagnostics(fit)[, c(
  "channel", "frequency_readout", "best_scale", "best_p_fwer",
  "supported_range", "curve_use"
)]
```

The selected scales are separated by target. `best_frequency` is the strongest
spatial-frequency readout, while `best_localization` is the strongest
location-wise scale-space evidence.

```{r selected-scale-targets}
fit$selected$best_frequency[, c("channel", "scale_label", "p_fwer", "curve_use")]
fit$selected$best_localization[, c("channel", "scale_label", "p_fwer", "curve_use")]
```

```{r resolution-curve-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Corrected evidence across the localization continuum. Higher values indicate stronger familywise-corrected evidence; the dashed line marks alpha = 0.10."}
plot_channels <- c("global_lowpass_energy", "global_band_energy", "local_energy")
plot_df <- subset(resolution, channel %in% plot_channels)
scale_df <- unique(plot_df[c("scale_index", "scale_label", "resolution_order")])
scale_df <- scale_df[order(scale_df$resolution_order), ]
plot_df$x <- match(plot_df$scale_index, scale_df$scale_index)
cols <- c(
  global_lowpass_energy = "#CC79A7",
  global_band_energy = "#009E73",
  local_energy = "#0072B2"
)
op <- par(mar = c(4.8, 4, 1, 1))
plot(NA, xlim = range(plot_df$x), ylim = c(0, max(plot_df$neg_log10_p, -log10(0.1)) * 1.15),
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "Resolution scale", ylab = expression(-log[10](p[FWER])))
for (ch in plot_channels) {
  d <- subset(plot_df, channel == ch)
  lines(d$x, d$neg_log10_p, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = cols[[ch]])
}
axis(1, at = seq_len(nrow(scale_df)), labels = scale_df$scale_label, las = 2)
abline(h = -log10(0.1), lty = 2, col = "firebrick")
legend("topright", legend = c("low-pass", "band-pass", "local energy"),
       col = cols[plot_channels], lwd = 2, pch = 19, bty = "n")
par(op)
```

A corrected point at a scale does not mean each voxel is significant. It means
that a localized test centered at that location and bandwidth has corrected
evidence. For local-energy display, use above-null energy summaries rather than
raw `z^2` maps.

For spatial-frequency interpretation, prefer `global_band_energy()`: its peak
is the band with strongest corrected evidence. `global_lowpass_energy()` is
cumulative, so coarse curves can remain strong even when the effect is not
confined to one band.

```{r energy-mass-summary}
mass <- energy_mass_map(fit)
range(as.numeric(mass), na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r energy-mass-checks, include = FALSE}
mass_vec <- as.numeric(mass)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(mass_vec)))
stopifnot(all(mass_vec >= 0))
stopifnot(abs(sum(mass_vec) - 1) < 1e-8 || sum(mass_vec) == 0)
```

```{r energy-mass-plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "The statistic image contains a broad planted effect. The energy-mass map shows where above-null scale-space energy is concentrated at the selected scale."}
mean_map <- Reduce("+", subject_images) / length(subject_images)
slice_at <- 6
slice_matrix <- function(x, z = slice_at) {
  matrix(as.numeric(x)[((z - 1) * prod(dims[1:2]) + 1):(z * prod(dims[1:2]))],
         nrow = dims[1])
}
draw_slice <- function(x, main, zlim = NULL, palette = hcl.colors(80, "Viridis")) {
  if (is.null(zlim)) zlim <- range(x, finite = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  image(seq_len(nrow(x)), seq_len(ncol(x)), x,
        col = palette, zlim = zlim, asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
        xlab = "", ylab = "", main = main)
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
draw_slice(slice_matrix(mean_map), "Mean subject contrast")
contour(seq_len(dims[1]), seq_len(dims[2]), slice_matrix(signal_mask),
        levels = 0.5, add = TRUE, drawlabels = FALSE,
        col = "white", lwd = 2)
draw_slice(slice_matrix(mass), "Above-null energy mass",
           palette = hcl.colors(80, "Inferno"))
contour(seq_len(dims[1]), seq_len(dims[2]), slice_matrix(signal_mask),
        levels = 0.5, add = TRUE, drawlabels = FALSE,
        col = "white", lwd = 2)
par(op)
```

For two-group analyses, `scale_space_twosample()` provides a simple label
permutation wrapper. For unbalanced clinical/control data or models with
nuisance covariates, prefer a GLM null generator.

```{r glm-null-example}
group <- factor(rep(c("control", "case"), each = 4), levels = c("control", "case"))
age <- seq_along(group)

glm_null <- null_glm(
  subject_images,
  design = ~ group + age,
  data = data.frame(group = group, age = age),
  contrast = "groupcase",
  n_perm = 19,
  seed = 2
)

glm_fit <- scale_space_energy(
  stat_vol = glm_null$stat_vol,
  mask = glm_null$mask,
  null_spec = glm_null,
  scales = scale_space(c(4, 8), include_global = TRUE, include_identity = TRUE),
  statistics = list(global_band_energy(), local_energy()),
  n_perm = 19
)

summary(glm_fit)
```

```{r glm-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(glm_null, "neurothresh_null_spec"))
stopifnot(inherits(glm_fit, "scale_space_energy_result"))
stopifnot(is.data.frame(summary(glm_fit)))
```

## What if you only have a statistic map?

You do not need to store all permutation maps in memory. If an upstream workflow
can regenerate the `b`th null statistic map, pass that deterministic draw
function directly.

```{r stat-map-plus-null-fun}
draw_null_map <- function(b) {
  glm_null$draw(b)
}

fit_from_function <- scale_space_energy(
  stat_vol = glm_null$stat_vol,
  mask = glm_null$mask,
  null_fun = draw_null_map,
  n_perm = glm_null$n_perm,
  scales = scale_space(c(4, 8), include_global = TRUE, include_identity = TRUE),
  statistics = list(global_lowpass_energy(), global_band_energy(), local_energy())
)

scale_space_diagnostics(fit_from_function)[, c(
  "channel", "frequency_readout", "best_scale", "best_p_fwer", "curve_use"
)]
```

The draw function must be deterministic by index: `draw_null_map(7)` should
return the same map every time. `scale_space_energy()` makes multiple passes
over the same null family to estimate null moments and then compute the
max-null distribution.

```{r stat-map-plus-null-spec}
external_null <- null_from_function(
  draw = draw_null_map,
  stat_vol = glm_null$stat_vol,
  mask = glm_null$mask,
  n_perm = glm_null$n_perm,
  kind = "external_stat_map_generator"
)

fit_from_null_spec <- scale_space_energy(
  external_null,
  scales = scale_space(c(4, 8), include_global = TRUE, include_identity = TRUE),
  statistics = list(global_band_energy(), local_energy())
)

summary(fit_from_null_spec)[, c("scale_label", "channel", "p_fwer", "curve_use")]
```

```{r stat-map-null-function-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(draw_null_map(3), draw_null_map(3)))
stopifnot(inherits(external_null, "neurothresh_null_spec"))
stopifnot(inherits(fit_from_function, "scale_space_energy_result"))
stopifnot(inherits(fit_from_null_spec, "scale_space_energy_result"))
```

If you already have precomputed null maps, use `null_from_maps()` instead. The
statistical requirement is the same in both cases: the observed map and every
null map must be produced by the same upstream statistic and must pass through
the same scale-space transforms before correction.

```{r stat-map-plus-null-maps}
stored_null_maps <- lapply(seq_len(glm_null$n_perm), draw_null_map)
maps_null <- null_from_maps(
  stat_vol = glm_null$stat_vol,
  null_maps = stored_null_maps,
  mask = glm_null$mask
)

fit_from_maps <- scale_space_energy(
  maps_null,
  scales = scale_space(8, include_global = TRUE, include_identity = TRUE),
  statistics = list(global_band_energy(), local_energy())
)

scale_space_diagnostics(fit_from_maps)[, c("channel", "best_scale", "best_p_fwer")]
```

```{r stat-map-null-maps-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(maps_null, "neurothresh_null_spec"))
stopifnot(inherits(fit_from_maps, "scale_space_energy_result"))
```

This approach is related to post-statistic spatial filtering methods such as
LISA: the same spatial operation is applied to observed and permuted maps before
inference. The distinction is that scale-space localized energy inference
searches a prespecified resolution family and uses max-null FWER over the full
search. It is therefore not smoothing until significance; the smoothing scales
are part of the corrected test family.
